---
title: "Difference-in-Differences: Placebo and Falsification Tests"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

## Motivation

Difference-in-differences estimates rely on identifying assumptions that cannot be directly tested.
Placebo and falsification tests provide indirect evidence on whether a DiD design is credible.

The key idea is simple: if we detect treatment effects where none should exist, the research design is likely invalid.

## Time-Placebo Tests

A time-placebo test assigns the treatment to a period before the actual intervention.
Under a valid parallel trends assumption, the estimated placebo effect should be close to zero.

## Simulated Panel Data

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)

set.seed(42)

n_units <- 60
time_periods <- -5:5

panel_data <- expand.grid(
  id = 1:n_units,
  time = time_periods
) %>%
  mutate(
    treated = ifelse(id <= n_units / 2, 1, 0),
    true_treatment_time = 0,
    outcome = 3 + 0.4 * time +
      treated * ifelse(time >= 0, 2, 0) +
      rnorm(n(), sd = 0.6)
  )
```

## Correct DiD Specification

We first estimate the DiD model using the correct treatment timing.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(fixest)

panel_data <- panel_data %>%
  mutate(post = ifelse(time >= 0, 1, 0))

did_correct <- feols(
  outcome ~ treated * post | id + time,
  data = panel_data
)

did_correct
```

## Time-Placebo DiD

We now assign the treatment to an earlier (placebo) period.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

panel_data <- panel_data %>%
  mutate(placebo_post = ifelse(time >= -3, 1, 0))

did_placebo <- feols(
  outcome ~ treated * placebo_post | id + time,
  data = panel_data
)

did_placebo
```

## Interpretation

In a credible design, the placebo DiD coefficient should be statistically insignificant and close to zero.

A significant placebo effect indicates a violation of the parallel trends assumption or other design flaws.

## Relation to Event Studies

Placebo tests are closely related to event-study diagnostics.
Both examine whether treatment effects appear before the actual intervention.
